subject: EdgeFin benchmark: post-call recap & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@edgefin.com>, Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFin benchmark: post-call recap & next steps

Hi John / Asha 

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of needs we captured:
- Target latency: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 350ms for 512-token generation (model TBD)
- Sustained throughput: ~30 req/sec for core inference workload
- Concurrency target: support up to 8 concurrent streaming sessions per instance
- Streaming requirement: chunked partial responses with token-level flush for low-latency UX
- Reproducibility: shared prompt set + deterministic seed where possible, clear measurement definitions

What I'll send by end of day: 
- Our benchmark methodology doc (attached) measurement definitions, test harness suggestions, and reproducibility checklist
- Example prompt set we typically use for finserv-style workloads (prompt_set_v1.jsonl)
- A proposed schedule for a 2-phase run: smoke (sanity) + sustained load run

Questions for you (so we can finalize scope):
1) Which model family do you want us to benchmark first (open-llama / llama-2 / redwood-verified?)
2) Can you share a representative subset of prompts or the file you mentioned during the call (we noted ~500 prompts, mix of short/long)?
3) Are you planning to run the benchmark in Redwood Hosted or in your Dedicated/Private environment?

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm model and provide sample prompts (EdgeFin sends sample_prompts.jsonl) action: EdgeFin
- We validate inputs and run smoke test on a reserved dedicated slot action: Redwood (Rafael)
- Run full benchmark and share reproducible artifact + dashboard action: Redwood (Marissa & Monica)

Attachments: benchmark_methodology_v1.pdf, prompt_set_v1.jsonl

Thanks talk soon.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: John Park <john.park@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@edgefin.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark: post-call recap & next steps

Marissa 

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Model: Let's start with an LLM equivalent to 30b-class performance; open model preferred but we're flexible if Redwood recommends a specific variant that matches production behaviour.
- Prompts: I'll attach a 200-sample subset now (edgefin_sample_prompts.jsonl) majority are short queries (~20-40 tokens) with a 20% tail of longer prompts (200-600 tokens)
- Target SLOs are as you listed; one nuance: p50 target should be measured for streaming-first UX (i.e., time-to-first-token + steady-state token generation should combine to p50 < 150ms for typical short prompts).

Operational asks: 
- We'd like the benchmark to measure server-side latency (excl. client network) and disambiguate time-to-first-byte for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints.
- Concurrency: we'll need to validate 8 concurrent sessions with independent KV caches to simulate multi-tenant behaviour.
- Reproducibility: please include the exact harness (Docker image or script) and the seed/config used.

Can Redwood reserve a dedicated slot for the smoke run next week (w/c 6 Jul)? If so, we can plan the full run the following week.

John
Head of Platform & Performance
EdgeFin
john.park@edgefin.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@edgefin.com>, Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark: post-call recap & next steps

John 

Great notes, thanks. Quick technical clarifications and what we'll provide in the methodology artifact: 

Measurement definitions (included in attached PDF):
- p50/p95/p99 latency: measured server-side inside our inference runtime (time from request receipt to final token(s) emitted), for streaming we report time-to-first-token (TTFT) and end-to-end time separately.
- Throughput: sustained successful requests/sec over a 5-minute window with target error rate < 1%.
- Concurrency: simultaneous in-flight requests; for streaming sessions we count active session streams.
- Tokenization and model config: we'll include tokenizer version, context window, and any quantization flags so results are reproducible.

Reproducibility deliverables we'll attach:
- A Dockerized harness (we'll share image tag) that runs the workload using your sample prompts; config file with fixed seeds; exact model weights / variant used for each run.
- Prompt set (prompt_set_v1.jsonl) with canonical IDs so you can re-run locally.
- A runbook describing env variables, hardware (GPU type), and kernel/config flags used.

About streaming: by default our streaming endpoint flushes partial tokens every 20-30ms at the runtime level; we'll surface TTFT (first partial token) and steady-state throughput. If you need different flush behavior we can tune runtime flags for the benchmark.

Scheduling: Rafael can provision a dedicated slot for a 2-hour smoke test next week (w/c 6 Jul). Proposed smoke test window: Tue 07 Jul 10:00-12:00 PT; full run: Thu 16 Jul 09:00-13:00 PT. Can you confirm availability?

I've attached prompt_set_v1.jsonl and the methodology PDF. Drive link for artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/edgefin-benchmark


Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: EdgeFin benchmark coordination / provisioning request

Team 

Looping you in to coordinate the EdgeFin benchmark. External ask: smoke test w/c 6 Jul (proposed Tue 07 Jul 10:00-12:00 PT), full run week of 13-17 Jul. Key requirements: 
- Reserved dedicated slot for smoke (2h) and full run (4h) with NVIDIA A100s (or equivalent)
- Ensure streaming endpoint config exposes TTFT metrics and allows token flush tuning
- Provide Docker image tag for harness; Rafael to coordinate image build & access (we'll publish to internal registry + provide credentials to EdgeFin)
- Instrumentation: trace IDs, per-request latency, per-token timestamps, and KV cache hit/miss metrics
- Owner assignments: Rafael (infra/provisioning), Monica (run ops & dashboard), Marissa (stakeholder comms)

Checklist before smoke run:
- Confirm GPU nodes availability & reserve capacity Rafael
- Validate harness on staging with sample_prompts Rafael
- Share access to drive folder and dashboards with EdgeFin Monica
- Confirm final prompt subset and model variant Marissa (waiting on EdgeFin reply)

Please confirm you can take these on and if any blockers. I'll chase EdgeFin to confirm the smoke window.

Marissa
Account Executive

From: John Park <john.park@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@edgefin.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark: post-call recap & next steps

Marissa / team 

Confirmed. Tue 07 Jul 10:00-12:00 PT works for the smoke. We'll provide the 200-sample subset (attached: edgefin_sample_prompts.jsonl) and a short doc outlining our expected multi-tenant KV behaviour.

A couple of final asks:
- Please include instructions for reproducing tokenization locally (we use a BPE variant tied to our preprocessor).
- If possible, when you run the smoke, could you capture TTFT distribution for the 90th percentile as well? We're particularly interested in the upper bucket for streaming start times.

Thanks looking forward to results.

John
Head of Platform & Performance, EdgeFin
john.park@edgefin.com
